text: I bought this device nearly one month ago. Now it's my time to give feedback. ✅ What’s working well The laptop delivers strong performance for everyday tasks: you can open multiple browser tabs, run productivity apps, and edit content, and it keeps up smoothly. It’s lightweight and well built: the build quality, solid keyboard feel, and good display are great for general content and brand work. Battery life is good but sometime for unknown reason it fails to meet expectation inspite of Intel evo certification . For a content-creator mindset (brand building, editing, general productivity), this machine gives you the tools — reliable keyboard, good display, good battery. --- ⚠️ What to keep in mind It’s not designed for heavy gaming or ultra-intensive graphics/3D rendering. The integrated graphics are decent for general use but will hit limits if you push into high-end video editing or dedicated GPU work,the system may feel overheating, lags. No big problems till now. So I am happy buying the device.

text: Have been using for the past 2 days. My usage has been mainly browsing internet, watching YouTube and movies. The display is amazing. The speakers are good enough for occassional personal use in a moderately quiet environment, I mostly use earphones, so it isn't much of a concern. Battery backup is also good, will last 6-7 hours easily on moderate usage. Opening of apps, tabs on chrome or other browsers is fast. Looks very good with it's thin build and metal chassis. The only issue till now is that it randomly heats up and throws out hot air from below, even when I am doing nothing except watching a YouTube video. Gets uncomfortable if it is on my lap and if it's on the bed or a table, the laptop itself gets hot as the vents are blocked. Don't know if it is a permanent flaw and how it will affect me in the long run. Otherwise a good buy for me, got it under 65K.
